angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 43,129,226 km at 122.40 pc = 4.71 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 55219: distance 122.399 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.021), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 122.399 +/- 2.57 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 7.9823 +/- 0.4825 mas (same row, RUWE 2.26), 16.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 61.994 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 55219: radius 61.994 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 1057.16 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.063) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 43,129,226 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4183 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 55219: effective temperature 4183 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.13) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 55219: effective temperature 4183 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.13) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * nu. UMa: spectral type K3-III: (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * nu. UMa: projected rotation speed 2.7 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 594) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.38 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 13 published values span log g 1.38 to 2.1, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...682A.145S)
